collect.bio: François Ruffin, born 18 October 1975 in Calais, is a journalist, documentary maker, essayist and politician. He founded the local newspaper Fakir in 1999 and directed the documentary Merci patron! (2016, César for best documentary 2017). He has been deputy for Somme's 1st constituency since 2017 and sat with the LFI group until 2024, though he never formally joined the party. He broke with Jean-Luc Mélenchon in July 2024, became president of Debout ! on 28 June 2025 and, per Wikipedia, announced a bid for the left primary and then a presidential run after that primary was cancelled.

offices.office: Deputy for Somme, 1st constituency (elected 2017, re-elected 2022 and 2024)
Secretary of the Economic Affairs Commission, Assemblée nationale

legal.case: Civil defamation ruling by the Amiens tribunal over statements in his book Quartier Nord about neighbourhood residents (Wikipedia describes him as found liable)
Victim, not accused: Mediapart reported LVMH hired Kyrnos (Bernard Squarcini) to surveil Ruffin and Fakir in 2015-2016. Arnault denied involvement. Judicial outcome unclear in the source.
HATVP reported a EUR 431,973 undervaluation of his audiovisual production company in his asset declaration. No criminal proceedings are reported in the source.

delivery.what: Merci patron! documentary (2016) on the LVMH/Arnault case, which won a César. Parliamentary work includes a high volume of amendments (4,098 rejected in the first year) and the SMIC-salary pledge, with most of his parliamentary pay passed to associations and the PCF.
delivery.assessment: Wikipedia reports high amendment volume but low early attendance (22% in his first year). Few of his own texts have been passed. I could not do a roll-call vote review or find any balanced outlet assessment because the web search budget ran out.

delivery.what: Initiated the Nouveau Front populaire coalition in June 2024 and then left LFI on 4 July 2024.
delivery.assessment: Described as a strategic split with Mélenchon. No outlet of differing lean was consulted.

traits.trait: Independent, populist-left, protectionist positioning bridging working-class and intellectual left
traits.evidence: Wikipedia summary of his stances and media portrayal. Only one source, so this does not meet the two-source threshold.

media_portrayal.neutral_media: Per Wikipedia: increasingly independent, bridging popular classes and the intellectual left. Criticised over low attendance, ethics episodes at Fakir (2017) and accusations of dog-whistles (2018) that he disputed.

verify.bio: François Ruffin, born 18 October 1975 in Calais, is a journalist, documentary maker, essayist and politician. He founded the newspaper Fakir in 1999 and directed the documentary Merci patron! (2016, César for best documentary 2017). He has been deputy for the Somme's 1st constituency since 2017, elected under the LFI label and sitting in the LFI group without being a formal party member; after breaking with Jean-Luc Mélenchon he left LFI on 4 July 2024 and joined the ecologist group (EcoS). He became president of Debout ! on 28 June 2025 and announced on 26 January 2026 that he was standing in the left primary. According to Wikipedia's Debout ! article, the primary was later cancelled and the party then planned to put him forward directly for the presidency.

offices.office: Deputy for Somme, 1st constituency (elected 2017, re-elected 2022 and 2024; LFI group 2017-2024, ecologist group from July 2024)
Secretary of the Economic Affairs Commission, Assemblée nationale

legal.case: Civil defamation suit at the Amiens tribunal over the portrayal of a resident in his 2006 book Quartier Nord. Wikipedia reports that he was found liable (condamné). No primary court source was available.

Ruffin was a victim, not a defendant. LVMH paid Bernard Squarcini's firm Kyrnos to surveil Ruffin and Fakir (March 2015 to February 2016). LVMH settled through a EUR 10 million CJIP, approved on 17 December 2021. On 7 March 2025 the Paris court convicted Squarcini, among other charges, and sentenced him to 4 years (2 of them custodial), a EUR 200,000 fine and a 5-year professional ban. His lawyers said he would appeal.
The HATVP observed that his asset declaration undervalued his audiovisual production company by EUR 431,973. This was an administrative observation, and no criminal proceedings are reported.

delivery.what: Directed the documentary Merci patron! (2016) about LVMH and Bernard Arnault, which won the 2017 César. As a deputy he tabled a high volume of amendments (4,098 in his first term, nearly all rejected). He keeps the net SMIC from his pay and gives about EUR 3,000 a month to associations. He also directed his public party-funding allocation to the PCF.
delivery.assessment: Wikipedia reports a high volume of amendments and commission interventions (162). It also reports low attendance in his first year: he was the least present LFI deputy at votes (22%), and he was among the least present in commission. Few texts of his own were adopted. No roll-call review and no assessment from outlets of different leanings could be obtained.

delivery.what: Called for a united left front in June 2024, which became the Nouveau Front populaire. He then left LFI on 4 July 2024 and joined the ecologist group.
delivery.assessment: Wikipedia describes it as a split with Mélenchon over a deep moral and electoral disagreement. No outlet of a different leaning was consulted.

media_portrayal.neutral_media: Per Wikipedia, outlets describe him as increasingly independent of LFI and as seeking to reconnect the left with working-class voters. Reported criticisms include low attendance in his first year, Fakir staff doubling as parliamentary collaborators (2017), and a 2018 Le Monde piece by Abel Mestre about ambiguous rhetorical references, which he disputed.
